questions.q: Who looked after Jim at the hall while the doctor and squire were away?
choices: Old Redruth, the gamekeeper
Mr. Dance, the supervisor
Jim's mother
Mr. Blandly, the squire's agent
questions.evidence: under the charge of old Redruth, the gamekeeper

questions.q: How did Jim spend his time while waiting at the hall?
choices: Dreaming over the map and imagining the island
Learning to sail a little boat on a nearby lake
Working long days at the Admiral Benbow
Studying medicine from the doctor's books
questions.evidence: I brooded by the hour together over the map

questions.q: What was the name of the ship the squire bought?
choices: The Hispaniola
The Spy-glass
The Royal George
The Walrus

questions.q: Why did Jim say Dr. Livesey would not like the squire's letter?
choices: The squire had told people they were going after treasure
The squire had spent far too much money on an old ship
The squire wrote that he had fallen ill in Bristol
The squire said the voyage would be put off until spring
questions.evidence: The squire has been talking, after all.

questions.q: The squire calls the bad things people say about Blandly "the most transparent calumnies." What are calumnies?
choices: False statements meant to hurt someone's name
Business deals made between ship owners
Kind compliments paid to a friend
Sailing orders written out for the whole of a ship's crew

questions.q: What job did the squire give Long John Silver?
choices: Ship's cook
Sailing master
First mate
Boatswain
questions.evidence: I engaged him on the spot to be ship's cook

questions.q: What did the squire say about Long John Silver's leg?
choices: He had lost it in his country's service
He had lost it to a shark off the coast
He had broken it falling from the mast
It had been hurt in a fight in a tavern
questions.evidence: he lost it in his country's service, under the immortal Hawke

questions.q: Silver helped choose the crew and got rid of some men the squire had already hired. Why might a careful reader be suspicious of this?
choices: Jim was warned about a one-legged seaman, and Silver is picking the crew
Silver was too young to know which sailors were any good
Silver had said he wanted to be the captain of the ship
The squire had ordered Silver to send those men away
questions.evidence: Long John even got rid of two out of the six or seven I had already engaged.

questions.q: Who found the competent man named Arrow to be the mate?
choices: Long John Silver
Mr. Blandly
Dr. Livesey
Old Tom Redruth, the gamekeeper
questions.evidence: Long John Silver unearthed a very competent man for a mate, a man named Arrow.

questions.q: What had the squire done for Jim's mother at the Admiral Benbow?
choices: Repaired the inn and found her a boy to help
Sold the inn for her and given her the money
Moved her into a room at the hall
Given her a share of the captain's treasure
questions.evidence: He had found her a boy as an apprentice also

questions.q: How did Jim feel when he saw the boy who would take his place at home?
choices: He saw he was really leaving home and cried for the first time
He was glad that someone else would now do all his chores
He was eager to teach the new boy kindly how to run the inn
He felt jealous and refused to speak to the boy at all
questions.evidence: I had my first attack of tears

questions.q: How did Jim and Redruth travel to Bristol after leaving the inn?
choices: By the mail coach from the Royal George
On horseback, riding all night beside Mr. Dance
By ship along the coast
On foot, walking all the way
questions.evidence: The mail picked us up about dusk at the Royal George on the heath.

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Getting ready for the voyage, leaving home, and reaching Bristol
The pirates coming back to attack the squire's hall in the dead of night
Jim finding the treasure hidden in the captain's sea-chest
The long voyage across the ocean to the treasure island
questions.evidence: The ship is bought and fitted.
